```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>x</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A <em>skyscapeR.sigTest</em> object created with <code>randomTest</code></p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>xrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Range of x-axis to plot.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>title</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Title to add to the plot.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>col</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Observed density colour. NULL uses the current style.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.pval</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical to control whether to print the global p-value. Default is TRUE.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.local</code></th><td><code>FALSE</code></td><td><p>Draw a separate panel on the same angular scale, with Excess and Deficit rows. Default FALSE. Symbols are ***, **, *, + and an open circle, with upper cutoffs 0.001, 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10. The open circle is centred at the same height as the stars and marks values above 0.10.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>pal</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Deficit and excess colours in that order. NULL uses the current style.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>...</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Additional arguments to be passed to <em>plot</em>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>obj</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>A skyObject or list of target groups for a density or significance plot. <code>"publication-mono"</code>. Monochrome uses grayscale and preserves line styles.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><p>A dash means the signature supplies no default expression. The function may resolve an omitted value internally.</p><h5>Return value</h5><p>Draws the empirical density and pointwise comparison envelope. Optional annotations display the global p-value and local regions.
</p>
```

### `pval2stars()` {#fn-pval2stars}

### `randomTest()` {#fn-randomtest}

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-randomtest)

```{=html}
<p>Following Silva (2020), the test combines the observed measurement densities into a summed probability density (SPD).
For each simulated dataset, the function draws one azimuth per measurement with replacement
from the uniform grid from 0 to 360 degrees at the source azimuth spacing. It applies the
source density family and measurement uncertainties and constructs a comparable SPD.
For a declination test, random azimuths are transformed using the site geometry; the
resulting null distribution in declination depends on latitude and horizon.
</p>
<p>A new transformation takes its atmosphere from <code>skyscapeR.vars</code>. A saved declination PDF supplies its original settings. The fit records these in metadata$atmosphere for declination tests.
</p>
```

**Study design and numerical checks.**

```{=html}
<p>The simulated null describes independently sampled orientations with the
specified site geometry and measurement model. It does not automatically model
shared construction episodes, correlated measurement errors, geographical
clustering or selection of sites after inspecting their orientations. Such
structure needs a justified sampling model or separate sensitivity analysis.
</p>
<p>The pointwise envelope is not a simultaneous confidence band. A significant
global result rejects the specified random-orientation model; it does not
identify a celestial target. Refine the comparison grid and increase
<code>nsims</code> to assess borderline results, preserving the seed and inputs.
More simulations improve Monte Carlo resolution, not the validity of the
archaeological sampling design. Repeated searches over alternative subsets or
models are not included in the within-fit local-cluster adjustment.
</p>



```

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Silva, F. (2020). A probabilistic framework and significance test for the analysis of structural orientations in skyscape archaeology. <em>Journal of Archaeological Science</em>, 118, 105138. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1016/j.jas.2020.105138")}.
</p>
<p>Silva, F. and Lomsdalen, T. (2025). ‘No easy way from the earth to the stars’: a new statistical approach to the orientation of the Maltese temples. <em>Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences</em>, 17, 96. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1007/s12520-025-02208-4")}.
</p>
<p>Maris, E. and Oostenveld, R. (2007). Nonparametric statistical testing of EEG- and MEG-data. <em>Journal of Neuroscience Methods</em>. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1016/j.jneumeth.2007.03.024")}.
</p>
<p>Sassenhagen, J. and Draschkow, D. (2019). Cluster-based permutation tests of MEG/EEG data do not establish significance of effect latency or location. <em>Psychophysiology</em>. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1111/psyp.13335")}.
</p>
<p>Dufour, J.-M. (2006). Monte Carlo tests with nuisance parameters: A general approach to finite-sample inference and nonstandard asymptotics. <em>Journal of Econometrics</em>, 133, 443-477. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.06.007")}.
</p>
<p>North, B. V., Curtis, D. and Sham, P. C. (2002). A note on the calculation of empirical P values from Monte Carlo procedures. <em>American Journal of Human Genetics</em>, 71, 439-441. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1086/341527")}.
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** Preserve the generating model, measurement-to-site mapping, simulation seed, comparison grid and rank convention. A change in the null answers a different archaeological question even when the same observed curve is used.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>pdf</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A <em>skyscapeR.pdf</em> object created with either <code>az.pdf</code> or <code>coordtrans</code></p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>az</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Original azimuth <em>skyscapeR.pdf</em>; required only when <code>pdf</code>
contains declination distributions. Must match its distribution count and
order. Do not supply this argument when <code>pdf</code> already contains azimuths.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>hor</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>For azimuth input, optionally supply one shared <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em>
to test in declination. For declination input, required: the original shared
horizon or an ordered list matching the distributions in <code>pdf</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>nsims</code></th><td><code>1000</code></td><td><p>Number of simulations, at least two. Default is 1000.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>conf</code></th><td><code>0.95</code></td><td><p>Confidence level as a fraction. For example, 0.95 requests a 95 percent envelope.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>tails</code></th><td><code>2</code></td><td><p>1 for upper excesses, 2 for excesses and deficits (default).</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>normalise</code></th><td><code>F</code></td><td><p>Logical to control whether to normalize SPDs. Default is FALSE</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.res</code></th><td><code>0.1</code></td><td><p>Resolution with which to output probability distribution(s). Default is 0.1 degrees.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>ncores</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Worker count. By default use half the detected available logical cores, rounded down with a minimum of one. Set ncores=1 for serial execution. The simulation count and memory batch size can further limit workers. Verbose output reports the effective count.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>T</code></td><td><p>Logical. Display progress or informational messages. Default <code>TRUE</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><p>A dash means the signature supplies no default expression. The function may resolve an omitted value internally.</p><h5>Return value</h5><p>A <em>skyscapeR.sigTest</em> list containing metadata (test settings,
global and local p-values) and data (empirical SPD and null confidence envelope).
No original PDFs or horizon objects are attached.
</p><h5>Study design and numerical checks</h5><p>The simulated null describes independently sampled orientations with the
specified site geometry and measurement model. It does not automatically model
shared construction episodes, correlated measurement errors, geographical
clustering or selection of sites after inspecting their orientations. Such
structure needs a justified sampling model or separate sensitivity analysis.
</p><p>The pointwise envelope is not a simultaneous confidence band. A significant
global result rejects the specified random-orientation model; it does not
identify a celestial target. Refine the comparison grid and increase
<code>nsims</code> to assess borderline results, preserving the seed and inputs.
More simulations improve Monte Carlo resolution, not the validity of the
archaeological sampling design. Repeated searches over alternative subsets or
models are not included in the within-fit local-cluster adjustment.
</p>
```
